```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(stringr)
library(kableExtra)

rm(list = ls())
if (rstudioapi::isAvailable()) {
  setwd(dirname(rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path))
}

# kableExtra 1.4.0 has a known bug (github.com/haozhu233/kableExtra/issues/831):
# any kable() piped into row_spec() gets its bookdown caption number
# duplicated in HTML output only, which also pushes every later table's
# number up by one. Forcing format="html" explicitly avoids it; PDF output
# already auto-detects "latex" correctly and isn't affected.
html_fmt <- function() if (knitr::is_html_output()) "html" else NULL

# row_spec(background = ...) emits \cellcolor in LaTeX, which needs colortbl; the
# bookdown PDF template loads xcolor without its table option, so request it.
if (knitr::is_latex_output()) invisible(kableExtra::usepackage_latex("colortbl"))

out_dir <- "../../output/5_inference_final"

# Shared labels/ordering, read from the same MWU comparison table report.Rmd
# uses, so both documents describe the same groups/models/methods.
comparison <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "empathy_group_comparison.csv"))
mechanism_names <- c(ER = "Emotional Reactions", IP = "Interpretations", EX = "Explorations")
mechanisms_used <- unique(comparison$mechanism)
models_used <- sort(unique(comparison$model))
methods_used <- sort(unique(comparison$method))

# Bayesian mixed-effects results (see 3c_bayesian_models.R).
bm_convergence <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "bayesian_convergence.csv"))
bm_convergence$converged <- as.logical(bm_convergence$converged)
bm_length_effect <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "bayesian_length_effect.csv"))
bm_vs_real <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "bayesian_contrasts_vs_real.csv"))
bm_vs_real_nolength_ip <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "bayesian_contrasts_vs_real_nolength_IP.csv"))
bm_between_model <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "bayesian_contrasts_between_model.csv"))
bm_within_model <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "bayesian_contrasts_within_model.csv"))

# Counts and weighted-vs-subsample numbers quoted in the methods, read from
# saved outputs rather than typed in. qc_filter_and_balance.csv has one row per
# (thread, model, method) cell with the synthetic count and the thread's real
# count; the weights in 3c_bayesian_models.R are min(1, real_count / cell size).
qc_cells <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "qc_filter_and_balance.csv"))
n_synth_all <- sum(qc_cells$original_n)
n_real <- sum(distinct(qc_cells, post_id, real_count)$real_count)
n_threads <- n_distinct(qc_cells$post_id)
n_synth_weight <- sum(pmin(qc_cells$original_n, qc_cells$real_count))
wcmp <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "stability_weighted_comparison.csv")) %>%
  mutate(diff_in_se = (weighted_estimate - subsample_mean_estimate) / subsample_mean_SE)
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")

# "Credible" here means both: pd > CREDIBLE_PD (the rough two-sided-p<0.05
# analogue - see intro) AND the 95% HPD interval for the odds ratio excludes
# 1. The two will usually agree; requiring both is a slightly more
# conservative flagging rule than either alone, deliberately, since pd alone
# can be extreme even for a tiny, practically negligible effect (pd depends
# only on which side of zero the posterior falls, not on effect size).
CREDIBLE_PD <- 0.975
is_credible <- function(df) df$pd > CREDIBLE_PD & (df$OR_LCL > 1 | df$OR_UCL < 1)

bm_convergence <- bm_convergence %>% mutate(mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism])
bm_length_effect <- bm_length_effect %>%
  mutate(mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism],
         direction = ifelse(log_length_coef > 0, "longer", "shorter"))
bm_vs_real <- bm_vs_real %>%
  mutate(mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism],
         direction = ifelse(odds_ratio < 1, "lower", "higher"),
         credible = is_credible(.))
bm_between_model <- bm_between_model %>% mutate(mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism], credible = is_credible(.))
bm_within_model <- bm_within_model %>% mutate(mechanism_label = mechanism_names[mechanism], credible = is_credible(.))

describe_rhat_margin <- function() {
  top <- bm_convergence %>% slice_max(max_rhat, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  sprintf("The largest max Rhat is %.4f (%s, %s); %d of %d fits are above 1.005, so several sit close to the 1.01 cutoff rather than well inside it.",
          top$max_rhat, top$mechanism_label, ifelse(top$model_stage == "A_group_omnibus", "Model A", "Model B"),
          sum(bm_convergence$max_rhat > 1.005), nrow(bm_convergence))
}

describe_convergence <- function() {
  ok <- bm_convergence %>% filter(converged)
  bad <- bm_convergence %>% filter(!converged)
  if (nrow(bad) == 0) {
    return("All six fits (Model A and Model B for all three mechanisms) converged cleanly: max Rhat < 1.01, minimum bulk-ESS ratio above 0.1, and zero divergent transitions throughout.")
  }
  bad_desc <- sprintf("**%s's %s** (%s)", bad$mechanism_label,
                       ifelse(bad$model_stage == "A_group_omnibus", "Model A", "Model B"),
                       bad$message)
  ok_desc <- if (nrow(ok) > 0) {
    sprintf(" %s converged cleanly.", toString(sprintf("%s's %s", ok$mechanism_label,
                                                          ifelse(ok$model_stage == "A_group_omnibus", "Model A", "Model B"))))
  } else ""
  sprintf("%s did not meet the convergence criteria (max Rhat < 1.01, min ESS ratio > 0.1, zero divergences).%s",
          toString(bad_desc), ok_desc)
}

# Whether the fit this whole document exists for - ER's Model B, which the
# frequentist clmm fit couldn't estimate at all (non-positive-definite
# Hessian, see report.Rmd) - actually produced usable results this time.
er_b_status <- function() {
  row <- bm_convergence %>% filter(mechanism == "ER", model_stage == "B_model_x_method")
  if (nrow(row) == 0) return("no result found for Emotional Reactions' Model B - check that 3c_bayesian_models.R actually ran that fit.")
  if (isTRUE(row$converged)) {
    "**this is the fit the frequentist model couldn't produce at all** - it now has a full posterior, credible intervals, and simple-effects contrasts below, none of which existed in the frequentist report."
  } else {
    sprintf("it still didn't meet the convergence criteria here either (%s) - weakly-informative priors alone weren't enough to fully resolve this fit's difficulty; see the discussion below before trusting its contrasts.", row$message)
  }
}

describe_length_significance_bayes <- function() {
  credible <- bm_length_effect %>% filter(pd > CREDIBLE_PD, !(CI_LCL < 0 & CI_UCL > 0))
  n <- nrow(bm_length_effect)
  if (nrow(credible) == n) return(sprintf("credibly nonzero for all %d mechanisms (pd > %.3f, 95%% CrI excludes 0)", n, CREDIBLE_PD))
  if (nrow(credible) == 0) return("not credibly nonzero for any mechanism at this threshold")
  sprintf("credibly nonzero for %s but not for %s", toString(credible$mechanism_label),
          toString(setdiff(bm_length_effect$mechanism_label, credible$mechanism_label)))
}

describe_length_direction_bayes <- function() {
  longer <- bm_length_effect$mechanism_label[bm_length_effect$direction == "longer"]
  shorter <- bm_length_effect$mechanism_label[bm_length_effect$direction == "shorter"]
  if (length(shorter) == 0) return(sprintf("in the same direction: %s all score higher with more words.", toString(longer)))
  if (length(longer) == 0) return(sprintf("in the same direction: %s all score lower with more words.", toString(shorter)))
  sprintf("not in the same direction: %s score higher with more words, while %s scores lower with more words.",
          toString(longer), toString(shorter))
}

describe_vs_real_summary_bayes <- function() {
  all_mechs <- unique(bm_vs_real$mechanism_label)
  higher <- bm_vs_real %>% filter(credible, direction == "higher")
  clean_mechs <- setdiff(all_mechs, unique(higher$mechanism_label))
  parts <- c()
  if (length(clean_mechs) > 0) {
    parts <- c(parts, sprintf("real scores credibly higher than every synthetic group for %s", toString(clean_mechs)))
  }
  if (nrow(higher) > 0) {
    exc <- higher %>% group_by(mechanism_label) %>%
      summarise(text = paste(sub(" - real", "", contrast), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
    parts <- c(parts, sprintf("%s %s the exception%s---%s score%s credibly *higher* than real",
                               toString(exc$mechanism_label), ifelse(nrow(exc) > 1, "are", "is"),
                               ifelse(nrow(exc) > 1, "s", ""), toString(exc$text),
                               ifelse(nrow(higher) > 1, "", "s")))
  }
  paste0(paste(parts, collapse = "; "), ".")
}

row_bg <- function(df) which(df$credible & df$odds_ratio > 1)
```

## Scope

This document is a **companion to [`report.Rmd`](report.html)**, not a
replacement for it - it only re-does the *mixed-effects modeling* stage
(originally `3b_mixed_effects_models.R`, fit with `ordinal::clmm` /
`lme4::glmer`), using `brms`/Stan instead. Everything else - the data
description, QC, and Mann-Whitney tests - lives in the main report; this
document doesn't repeat it.

**Why:** on the full dataset, Emotional Reactions' Model B (the model x
method interaction) fails to converge under maximum likelihood - the fit's
Hessian is not positive definite, so no valid standard error or p-value
exists for it at all (see `report.Rmd`'s convergence discussion). The usual
frequentist fix for this kind of separation, Firth-style penalized
likelihood, has no mature implementation that supports *both* an ordinal
cumulative-link outcome and a random intercept for post-clustering, in R or
Python (checked directly: `ordinal::clm`/`clmm` have no bias-reduction
option; `brglm2` only covers fixed-effects GLMs with no cumulative-link
family). A Bayesian fit with weakly-informative priors resolves the same
separation problem the same way Firth's correction does - by keeping
estimates finite instead of letting them run to a boundary - while keeping
the interaction and the `post_id` random intercept intact.

**Data and response weights.** All `r fmt(n_real + n_synth_all)` comments are
modeled (`r fmt(n_real)` real, `r fmt(n_synth_all)` synthetic, from
`r fmt(n_threads)` threads): no length-outlier exclusion and no random
subsampling (both were examined and rejected; see
`report_outlier_exclusion`). Synthetic comments outnumber real ones within a
thread, because they were generated against each thread's total comment count
while the real comments are a smaller clinician-only subset. To stop long
threads from counting for more on the synthetic side than on the real side,
each real comment gets weight 1 and each synthetic comment gets
`w = min(1, real count / synthetic count)` for its (thread, model, method)
cell. The synthetic weights sum to `r fmt(n_synth_weight)` - exactly what
per-thread subsampling would keep - and the expected subsampled
log-likelihood equals the weighted one, so a weighted fit targets the
average over random subsamples without depending on any single draw.

`brms` multiplies each comment's log-likelihood by its weight, so this is a
pseudo-likelihood: point estimates target the same quantity as subsampling,
but posterior widths are approximate (they behave as if the sum of the
weights were the sample size) and are not corrected for the weighting. A
check that a fit with weight 2 on every comment matches an unweighted fit on
the doubled data confirmed the weights enter the likelihood as intended. In a
separate frequentist check on Interpretations and Explorations (50 balanced
subsamples vs. one weighted fit), the weighted estimates sat a median of
`r sprintf("%.2f", median(abs(wcmp$diff_in_se)))` SE from the subsample
average (up to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(abs(wcmp$diff_in_se)))` SE), and the
weighted fit's naive standard errors were about
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (median(wcmp$se_ratio_weighted_over_subsample) - 1))`% larger
than a single subsample's. The weighted fit is therefore a different
estimator, not an exact stand-in for subsampling, and that check did not
cover Emotional Reactions. Subsampling sensitivity checks are planned
separately.

**Models**, fit separately for each mechanism, with weights `w` as above:

- **A** (`label | weights(w) ~ group + log(length) + (1|post_id)`, all
  comments): each (model, method) group vs. real.
- **B** (`label | weights(w) ~ model * method + log(length) + (1|post_id)`,
  synthetic comments only): simple-effects contrasts between models within
  each method, and between methods within each model.

Emotional Reactions uses `family = cumulative("logit")` (all 3 empathy
levels); Interpretations and Explorations use `family = bernoulli("logit")`
on `label == 2` (both never predict label 1 in this data - same as the
frequentist version).

**Priors:** `normal(0, 2.5)` on every fixed effect and (for Emotional
Reactions) the ordinal thresholds - a standard weakly-informative default for
logistic-type models (Gelman, Jakulin, Pittau & Su, 2008) - and
`student_t(3, 0, 2.5)` on the `post_id` random-effect SD (brms's own
default). This is what actually addresses separation: brms's *default*
fixed-effect prior is an improper flat prior, which would leave the same
non-identifiability problem the frequentist fit has.

**Sampler and reproducibility:** `brms`/Stan via `cmdstanr`, 4 chains of 2000
iterations (1000 warmup), with 4 threads per chain. The Interpretations and
Explorations Model A fits were rerun with 4000 iterations (same warmup)
because their max Rhat was 1.011 at 2000. The seed (20260101) is fixed, but
within-chain threading makes exact reproduction of the draws from the seed
alone unreliable (identical seeds with threading gave different draws in a
direct test, because multithreaded summation order is not deterministic). The
fitted models, including every posterior draw, are saved to disk
(`models_bayesian/`), with the software versions and settings in
`run_metadata.txt`; reproducibility rests on those saved fits, not on
regenerating identical draws.

**Reading this document vs. the frequentist one:** there is no p-value in a
Bayesian fit. In place of BH-adjusted p-values, contrasts below report a 95%
highest-posterior-density (HPD) credible interval and `pd`, the posterior
*probability of direction* - the share of posterior draws on the same side
of zero as the point estimate. `pd` and a p-value answer different
questions and aren't interchangeable, but as a rough calibration, `pd >
0.975` is comparable to two-sided `p < 0.05` (Makowski et al., 2019). A
contrast is called **credible** below only when *both* `pd > 0.975` **and**
the 95% CrI for the odds ratio excludes 1 - deliberately a bit more
conservative than either alone, since `pd` can be extreme even for a tiny,
practically negligible effect. Contrasts are odds ratios (link-scale
estimates, exponentiated).

## Convergence

```{r bm-convergence}
bm_convergence %>%
  select(mechanism_label, model_stage, model_type, converged, max_rhat, min_neff_ratio, divergent_transitions) %>%
  kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 3, 0),
        col.names = c("Mechanism", "Model", "Family", "Converged", "Max Rhat", "Min ESS ratio", "Divergences"),
        caption = "Convergence for each brms fit: max Rhat < 1.01, minimum bulk-ESS ratio above 0.1, and zero divergent transitions.")
```

`r describe_convergence()` `r describe_rhat_margin()`

Emotional Reactions' Model B is the fit this document exists to try to
rescue - `r er_b_status()`

## Comment length

```{r bm-length}
bm_length_effect %>%
  select(mechanism_label, log_length_coef, CI_LCL, CI_UCL, pd) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Mechanism", "log(length) coef.", "95% CrI (low)", "95% CrI (high)", "pd"),
        caption = "Model A: posterior median log(length) coefficient (logit scale), with its credible interval and probability of direction.")
```

Comment length (log-transformed) is `r describe_length_significance_bayes()`,
and `r describe_length_direction_bayes()`

## Real vs. synthetic (Model A)

```{r bm-vs-real}
vs_real_df <- bm_vs_real %>%
  mutate(contrast = sub(" - real", "", contrast)) %>%
  select(mechanism_label, contrast, odds_ratio, OR_LCL, OR_UCL, pd, credible)

vs_real_df %>%
  select(-credible) %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = c(0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 3),
        col.names = c("Mechanism", "Group", "Odds ratio", "OR 95% CrI (low)", "OR 95% CrI (high)", "pd"),
        caption = "Model A: each (model, method) group vs. real (odds ratio below 1 = lower odds of higher empathy than real; credible rows with OR above 1 shaded).") %>%
  row_spec(row_bg(vs_real_df), background = "#f8d7da")
```

`r describe_vs_real_summary_bayes()`

```{r bm-length-confound-ip}
describe_length_confound_ip_bayes <- function() {
  ip_vs_real <- bm_vs_real %>% filter(mechanism == "IP") %>% select(contrast, direction)
  nolength_dir <- bm_vs_real_nolength_ip %>%
    mutate(direction_nolength = ifelse(odds_ratio < 1, "lower", "higher")) %>%
    select(contrast, direction_nolength)
  flips <- ip_vs_real %>% inner_join(nolength_dir, by = "contrast") %>%
    filter(direction != direction_nolength)
  if (nrow(flips) == 0) {
    return("Refitting Interpretations' Model A without `log(length)` doesn't flip any group's direction, so the pattern above isn't a length artifact under this model either.")
  }
  sprintf("Refitting Interpretations' Model A without `log(length)` flips the posterior median direction for %s (%d group%s), consistent with a length confound rather than a pure model/method effect for those groups.",
          toString(sub(" - real", "", flips$contrast)), nrow(flips), ifelse(nrow(flips) > 1, "s", ""))
}
```

`r describe_length_confound_ip_bayes()`

## Simple-effects contrasts (Model B)

Same rationale as the frequentist report: rather than pooled main-effect
means (which would be misleading wherever the model x method interaction is
credible), two sets of simple-effects contrasts - models compared within
each method, and methods compared within each model.

```{r bm-between-model}
between_df <- bm_between_model %>% select(mechanism_label, method, contrast, odds_ratio, OR_LCL, OR_UCL, pd, credible)
between_df %>%
  select(-credible) %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 3),
        col.names = c("Mechanism", "Method", "Contrast", "Odds ratio", "OR 95% CrI (low)", "OR 95% CrI (high)", "pd"),
        caption = "Model B: pairwise model contrasts within each method.") %>%
  row_spec(row_bg(between_df), background = "#f8d7da")
```

```{r bm-within-model}
within_df <- bm_within_model %>% select(mechanism_label, model, contrast, odds_ratio, OR_LCL, OR_UCL, pd, credible)
within_df %>%
  select(-credible) %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 3),
        col.names = c("Mechanism", "Model", "Contrast", "Odds ratio", "OR 95% CrI (low)", "OR 95% CrI (high)", "pd"),
        caption = "Model B: pairwise method contrasts within each model.") %>%
  row_spec(row_bg(within_df), background = "#f8d7da")
```

```{r bm-missing-check}
describe_bayes_vs_freq_coverage <- function() {
  freq_missing_er <- TRUE  # ER's Model B was entirely absent from report.Rmd's simple-effects tables
  n_er_between <- sum(bm_between_model$mechanism == "ER")
  n_er_within <- sum(bm_within_model$mechanism == "ER")
  if (n_er_between > 0 && n_er_within > 0) {
    "Unlike the frequentist report - where Emotional Reactions was entirely absent from both simple-effects tables because its Model B fit was unusable - Emotional Reactions appears in both tables above."
  } else {
    "Emotional Reactions is still missing from one or both tables above, which would mean this Bayesian fit didn't fully resolve the frequentist model's problem either - check the convergence section before trusting any partial results."
  }
}
```

`r describe_bayes_vs_freq_coverage()`
